answer: Embodied Energy Ledger. Each identity must submit a hardware-rooted power trace: a meter attests joules actually dissipated by its own compute over time, signed by a per-device key fused at manufacture. Admission requires the identity's energy draw to match its claimed work within a tight ratio, rechecked at each dawn. A zephyr of fabricated traces fails cross-consistency: real silicon's thermal and current curves can't be simulated cheaper than running it. A quartz clock binds each meter's timestamps to attested drift, so replaying another device's trace breaks.
